thesis: Visibility is not a neutral good — it is a governance technology whose costs fall unevenly.

sections.title: The promise of visibility
sections.function: Set up the commonplace the essay complicates
sections.entry: The reader treats being seen as uncomplicatedly empowering
sections.exit: The reader suspects visibility has a price list

claims.text: Contemporary platforms frame visibility as the default route to recognition.
Visibility regimes distribute the burden of being seen unevenly across groups.

sections.title: What the ledger hides
sections.entry: Visibility is a demand before it is a gift
sections.exit: The reader can name who audits whom

claims.text: The demand to be visible doubles as a demand to be legible to power.
Opting out of visibility is itself read as a political act.

sections.title: Selective opacity
sections.entry: The reader accepts the audit asymmetry
sections.exit: The reader holds a criterion for when to refuse the stage

claims.text: Strategic opacity is a defensible posture, not a retreat.

alternativesConsidered: A historical genealogy of surveillance — rejected: the thread's material is normative, not archival.
A platform-critique frame — rejected: it narrows the argument to one industry.

gaps.needed: A first-person example of refusing visibility that only the author can supply
